newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepali authorities search for killer wildcat.
newsitem.headline: Nepali authorities search for killer wildcat.

text.p: Authorities in western Nepal have ordered the killing of a big cat which has mauled about 50 people to death in recent months, officials said on Monday.
"We have given standing orders to shoot the beast," Sthaneswar Devakota, the chief district officer in the region of Baitadi, told Reuters.
State-owned RSS news agency on Monday quoted local villagers as saying a tiger had killed up to 50 people, most of them young children, in the last five months.
But Devakota suspected a leopard which had killed 35 people since December 1994 in the area may be the culprit.
RSS said the beast had unleashed a "considerable degree of terror" in the district, taking shelter under thatched roofs and attacking people, most of them children, when they were alone.
"It is difficult for the police to spot the animal, which hides in the jungles and caves," Devakota said.
